Start checks printed `engineer` and `DAEO-n0wb` from printenv, and git gave `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-92` on `w2/W2-92`. `python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` printed `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-92/src/gov/__init__.py`. The main repository's hooks folder holds only `*.sample` files. The record contains no 40-hex hash.
tests: none run (a record-only task)
discoveries: (1) Totals, both figures together: the control (`7ca16b19df3f`) has hit@5 at 11 of 20 (55 %), 30 points short of CAP-10's floor of 85 and 40 short of the 95 % target, with full evidence at 11 of 20 (55 %), 44 points short of 99 %, and 15 of 20 in the bundle. The head (`fb0c8c430171`) has hit@5 at 10 of 20 (50 %), short by 35 and 45, with full evidence at 12 of 20 (60 %), short by 39, and 15 of 20 in the bundle. The control equals W2-86's tree-code head on every cell except Q08's rank (11 there, 10 here). (2) The record route takes Q01 (DEC-782 by id, the only new start), Q06 (W2-54 → DAEO-0rfi), Q07 (DAEO-0mab, by its title) and Q14 (W2-03 → DAEO-ym8a). The last three are already asked with `--ticket`, so the route adds nothing for them and moves no figure. (3) The code route takes a word in 15 of 20 questions: Q02 and Q04–Q12, plus Q14 and Q16–Q19. Q10 went from 0 to 2 of 2 pieces (rank 6, now in the bundle; hit@5 still no). Q11 went from 1 to 2 of 2 pieces (hit@5 still yes, rank 4). In both, the callers' spans cover the gold calling lines. For Q17, the plain words `search` (three functions) and `embedded` were taken: hit@5 went from yes to no (rank 2 → 21, out of the bundle) and full evidence stayed no at 1 of 2. For Q09 (`context`), hit@5 stayed no and full evidence went from 1 to 0 of 1 (rank 44 → none). Q08's rank went up from 10 to 8 with no reason in the records. For Q14 the rank went from 17 to 16 and the pieces from 4 to 3 of 9. For Q18 the pieces went from 0 to 1 of 2 (rank 61); the found piece is probably the PreCompact hook's call to `record.write` at line 112, but this is not shown. (4) The code route's definition rule also matches prose: in Q05, "and" is taken because a docstring line of `src/gov/cli/main.py` (line 5) begins "class and". It is harmless there (the stacked digest is unchanged), but the rule reads `def`/`class` inside docstrings. (5) The head run took 2,552 s against the control's 770 s: 72 calls against 52, and 35.4 s per call against 14.8 s. Every call (each continuation page is stateless) reruns the code route, which reads all 150 code files and, for 15 questions, starts a session of the code-graph tool.
risks: §6 of the record reads each route's work from the head code's rules applied to the question text and the store (opened immutable), not from the records, which hold no items or facets. So the causes given for Q17, Q09 and Q18 are labelled "likely", not shown. Each measure was run once, with no repeat.
lessons: The records can't tell you why a figure moved. They don't keep the stacked items, the per-route facets, per-call times or the load. Keeping each run's first-call paths, or `gov retrieve --json` spot outputs for the questions that moved, would let the next record show causes instead of inferring them. Also, `gov retrieve` in this worktree answers FACET_UNAVAILABLE because the lexical and semantic stores are stale. I used it once, for DEC-833's two figures, got no evidence, and read W2-61's and W2-86's records directly.
proposed_decisions: The code route's `_defined` should ignore prose and match only real definitions (for example by asking the code graph, or by skipping docstrings), and it should not rerun on every continuation page. I recommend raising this as a gap row; confidence medium.
unresolved: The records cannot tell me: why the head rebuild's first try exited 69; why Q08 moved up; which items outrank Q17's gold; what displaced Q09's piece; which of Q18's pieces was found; how the extra run length divides between the code route and machine load; and whether the code graph holds nested functions such as `embedded`. The disk gate readings were not logged.
recommended_next_action: The lead should judge KPI 5 against its failure line with the Q17 and Q09 losses in view, and decide whether the code route's plain-word rule needs a repair batch before the audit.
